binders: For every natural number m, including m = 0.
For every function q : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ^m, represented as q(x,t)(i) with i ∈ Fin m; the first real argument is the spatial integration variable and the second is the differentiation variable.
For every function flux : ℝ^m → ℝ^m; it takes the whole state vector and may couple its coordinates.
Within both equivalent conditions, for every x₁, x₂, t ∈ ℝ, with no ordering restriction on x₁ and x₂.
The variable x is bound by the spatial integral, and τ is the argument of the function differentiated at t. Both endpoints remain fixed during differentiation.
There are no existentially quantified witnesses.
hypotheses: There are no additional hypotheses on m, q, or flux beyond their types. The displayed integrability and derivative requirements are inside the equivalent predicates.
conclusions: LocalDef001(q,flux) holds if and only if, for every real x₁, x₂, t, the spatial function x ↦ q(x,t) is integrable on both (x₁,x₂] and (x₂,x₁] with respect to μ = Real.measureSpace.volume, and the vector-valued function τ ↦ ∫ from x₁ to x₂ q(x,τ) dμ(x) has derivative flux(q(x₁,t)) − flux(q(x₂,t)) at t.
After expanding LocalDef001 and LocalDef002, the equivalence has identical mathematical conditions on its two sides.
mathematical_definitions: The state space ℝ^m is the function space Fin m → ℝ, with pointwise vector operations, the finite product normed-space structure, and the product of the usual real topologies.
Write μ for the distinguished measure selected by Real.measureSpace.volume. Its construction and normalization are not expanded in the supplied packet.
For fixed endpoints a and b, define Iₐᵦ(τ) = ∫_(a,b] q(x,τ) dμ(x) − ∫_(b,a] q(x,τ) dμ(x), using vector-valued integrals.
Interval integrability at time t means integrability of x ↦ q(x,t) on both (a,b] and (b,a]. Equivalently, it means integrability on (min(a,b),max(a,b)].

The derivative requirement is the ordinary two-sided vector derivative Iₐᵦ′(t) = flux(q(a,t)) − flux(q(b,t)); equivalently, the norm of Iₐᵦ(t+h) − Iₐᵦ(t) − h[flux(q(a,t)) − flux(q(b,t))], divided by |h|, tends to zero as nonzero h tends to zero.
In each coordinate i < m, the derivative value is flux(q(a,t))(i) − flux(q(b,t))(i).
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every finite dimension m and arbitrary functions q assigning an m-component real state to each real spatial point and real time, and flux assigning an m-component real vector to each state, LocalDef001(q,flux) is equivalent to the following condition: at every real time and for every pair of real spatial endpoints, the state is integrable between those endpoints with respect to the designated real measure, and the ordinary time derivative of its oriented spatial integral equals the flux evaluated at the first endpoint's state minus the flux evaluated at the second endpoint's state. LocalDef001 is itself defined to be exactly this condition through LocalDef002, so the proposition unfolds a definition rather than asserting that arbitrary q and flux satisfy this condition.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The theorem asserts an equivalence for arbitrary q and flux; it does not assert either equivalent condition unconditionally.
The dimension is finite but may be zero. For m = 0 the state space has one element, all vector values are zero, and both integrability and derivative conditions hold trivially.
Endpoints may occur in either order. The integral is oriented, and the flux difference uses the corresponding first-minus-second order.
For equal endpoints the integration domains are empty, the integral is identically zero, and the endpoint flux difference is zero, so that instance of the condition is automatic.
Space and time both range over all of ℝ. There is no restricted spatial domain, finite time interval, or one-sided initial-time derivative.
Integrability is required on every bounded spatial interval at every time; integrability on the entire real line and joint space-time integrability are not required.
The derivative is required at every real time, not merely almost everywhere or in a distributional sense.
No continuity, differentiability, or measurability of flux is separately imposed. No pointwise spatial or temporal differentiability of q is separately imposed.
The formula uses actual endpoint values of q and flux(q), not boundary traces or equivalence classes modulo almost-everywhere equality.
Flux is a total function of the entire state vector, with no explicit spatial or temporal argument and no specified admissible-state subset.
No pointwise partial differential equation, distributional formulation, initial data, boundary conditions, entropy condition, existence theorem, or uniqueness theorem is encoded.
ambiguities: D060 supplies only inferInstance for Real.measureSpace. Thus the packet fixes a particular installed measure but does not expose enough of its construction to independently verify that it is Lebesgue measure with the usual normalization. The translation retains that measure as μ rather than inferring its normalization from its name.
